Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\sigma(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\sigma(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\},\ |J|=n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\rho_i(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be an orthonormal family in a real or complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), and
for $x\in H$ and finite $F\subseteq I$ put

$$P_Fx:=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i .$$

Then the following four assertions are equivalent:

1. **(completeness)** the closed linear span of $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ is $H$;
2. **(zero complement)** the only vector orthogonal to every $e_i$ is $0$;
3. **(Parseval)** $\displaystyle\sum_{i\in I}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2=\|x\|^2$
   for every $x\in H$, the sum being the supremum of the finite subsums
   ([[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]);
4. **(net convergence)** the finite-subset net $(P_Fx)_{F\in\operatorname{Fin}(I)}$
   converges to $x$ for every $x\in H$.

Assertion 2 is the statement
$\operatorname{span}\{e_i : i\in I\}^\perp=\{0\}$
([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $T$ be a
densely defined linear operator on $H$, with domain $D(T)$ dense in $H$
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]], [[def-dense-top]]).
Since $D(T)$ is dense, and since $H$ is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]), every
bounded linear functional on the normed space $(D(T),\|\cdot\|)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) extends uniquely to a bounded linear
functional $\widetilde\varphi$ on $H$ of the same norm, by setting
$\widetilde\varphi(z)=\lim_n\varphi(z_n)$ for any sequence $z_n\in D(T)$ with
$z_n\to z$ in $H$; the limit exists because $\varphi$ is bounded on a dense
subspace and $H$ is complete, and it does not depend on the sequence because a
bounded functional is uniformly continuous.

A vector $y\in H$ belongs to the **adjoint domain** $D(T^*)$ when the linear
functional $\varphi_y:D(T)\to\mathbb C$, $\varphi_y(x)=\langle Tx,y\rangle$, is
bounded on $(D(T),\|\cdot\|)$. In that case Hilbert space Riesz representation
([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) applied to the extension
$\widetilde{\varphi_y}$ produces a unique vector $T^*y\in H$ with
$$T^*y\text{ is the unique }w\in H\text{ such that }\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,w\rangle\quad\text{for all }x\in D(T),$$
equivalently $\widetilde{\varphi_y}(z)=\langle z,T^*y\rangle$ for all $z\in H$.
The map $T^*:D(T^*)\to H$, $y\mapsto T^*y$, is the **adjoint** of $T$.

**Well-definedness.** The functional $\varphi_y$ is linear in $x$ for each
$y$, so its domain of boundedness $D(T^*)$ is a linear subspace: if
$\varphi_y,\varphi_{y'}$ are bounded so is $\varphi_{ay+by'}$ for scalars
$a,b$, because the first-variable-linear convention gives
$\varphi_{ay+by'}=\overline a\,\varphi_y+\overline b\,\varphi_{y'}$. On
$D(T^*)$ the map $T^*$ is linear: if $y,y'$ are represented by $w,w'$, then
$ay+by'$ is represented by $aw+bw'$, since
$\langle x,aw+bw'\rangle=\overline a\langle x,w\rangle+
\overline b\langle x,w'\rangle$; the representing vector is unique. By Riesz representation for the Hilbert space
$H$ a vector $w\in H$ is determined by the values $\langle z,w\rangle$ with
$z$ ranging over $H$, and those values are determined by the functional
$\widetilde{\varphi_y}$. Equivalently, if $w,w'$ both represent $\varphi_y$,
then $\langle x,w-w'\rangle=0$ for every $x\in D(T)$; density of $D(T)$ and
continuity of the inner product extend this equality to every $x\in H$, and
taking $x=w-w'$ gives $w=w'$. Finally only
ambient-norm boundedness of $\varphi_y$ on $D(T)$ is required: no extension,
no closure and no closedness of $T$ is presupposed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $T$ be a densely defined linear operator on $H$.

- $T$ is **symmetric** when $T\subseteq T^*$, that is, $D(T)\subseteq D(T^*)$ and
  $Tx=T^*x$ for all $x\in D(T)$; equivalently
  $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y\in D(T)$.
- $T$ is **self-adjoint** when $T=T^*$, that is, the domains and the values
  agree.
- $T$ is **essentially self-adjoint** when its closure $\overline T$ is
  self-adjoint; by [[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]] this presupposes
  that $T$ is closable.

**Consequences, with proofs.** These are part of the content of the definition.

1. *A symmetric $T$ is closable.* $T\subseteq T^*$ and $T^*$ is closed
   ([[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]]), so $T^*$ is a closed
   extension of $T$. In particular the closure $\overline T$ exists and
   $\overline T\subseteq T^*$.
2. *The closure of a symmetric operator is symmetric.* If $T\subseteq T^*$,
   the inclusion reversal of
   [[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]] applied to
   $T\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq T^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$. Applying it once more to the inclusion
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq(T^{**})^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^{***}$. Since $\overline T=T^{**}$ and
   $(\overline T)^*=T^{***}$
   ([[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]]), this reads
   $\overline T\subseteq(\overline T)^*$: the closure is symmetric. (Each
   application is legitimate because the adjoint is defined once its operator
   is densely defined, and $D(T^{**})$ is dense because
   $T\subseteq T^{**}=\overline T$, so that $D(T^{**})$ contains the dense
   domain $D(T)$.)
3. *A self-adjoint operator has no proper symmetric extension.* If $T=T^*$ and
   $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*$, then $S^*\subseteq T^*$ by inclusion reversal,
   so $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*\subseteq T^*=T$ and all inclusions are
   equalities.
4. *A self-adjoint operator is closed*, being equal to the adjoint $T^*$ of the
   densely defined $T$, and *an essentially self-adjoint operator has exactly
   one self-adjoint extension*, namely $\overline T$: a self-adjoint extension
   $S$ of $T$ is closed, hence contains the least closed extension
   $\overline T$, and then $S\subseteq S^*\subseteq(\overline T)^*=\overline T$
   by item 2 and symmetry, so $S=\overline T$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a projection valued measure on the
measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on the complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be
$\Sigma$-measurable. Put
$$D(f(E)):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_X|f|^2\,dE_x<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,$$
where the scalar measures $E_x$ are those of
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]], and for $x\in D(f(E))$ set
$$f(E)x:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\Phi_E\bigl(f\,\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}\bigr)x,$$
For $H\ne\{0\}$, the bounded integrals $\Phi_E$ are those of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], and the limit is taken in the norm of $H$.
For $H=\{0\}$, define $\Phi_E(g)$ to be the unique operator on $H$ for every bounded measurable $g$. Then $E_0$ is the zero measure, $D(f(E))=H$, and $f(E)0=0$. Thus this case is defined directly without applying a theorem requiring a nonzero space.

**Well-definedness.** $D(f(E))$ is a linear subspace: the estimate
$E_{x+y}\le2E_x+2E_y$ for scalar measures and $E_{\alpha x}=|\alpha|^2E_x$
follow from $\|E(B)(x+y)\|^2\le2\|E(B)x\|^2+2\|E(B)y\|^2$ and
$\|E(B)\alpha x\|^2=|\alpha|^2\|E(B)x\|^2$. Writing $f_n:=f\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}$
the sets $\{|f|\le n\}$ are measurable, so $f_n$ is bounded and measurable.
For $m,n\ge N$,
$$|f_n-f_m|^2\le |f|^2\mathbf1_{\{|f|>N\}}.$$
The integral of the right side against $E_x$ tends to zero by
[[thm-dominated-convergence]], with the integrable majorant $|f|^2$ and
pointwise limit zero since $f$ is finite-valued. Linearity of the bounded
calculus ([[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]]) and its quadratic identity give
$$\|\Phi_E(f_n)x-\Phi_E(f_m)x\|^2=\int|f_n-f_m|^2\,dE_x.$$
These clauses hold directly on the zero space as well. Hence the truncation
vectors are Cauchy and converge uniquely by Hilbert-space completeness
([[def-hilbert-space]]). The limit is linear in $x$ because every truncation
operator is linear and addition and scalar multiplication are norm-continuous.
Countable Choice is inherited from the bounded PVM suppliers; no further
choice is needed to take these specified limits.

Finally, if two $\Sigma$-measurable functions $f,g$ agree outside a measurable
set $N$ with $E(N)=0$, then $E_x(N)=\|E(N)x\|^2=0$ for every $x$. Thus the
integrals of $|f|^2$ and $|g|^2$ agree, so their domains agree. At every
truncation level their bounded truncations agree outside $N$; the quadratic
identity applied to the difference gives equal truncation vectors for every
$x$. Taking limits gives $f(E)x=g(E)x$ on their common domain.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$
on the complex Hilbert space $H$ and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be $\Sigma$-measurable. Then the
operator $f(E)$ of [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]] is densely defined
and closed, and it is normal, in the sense $D(f(E))=D(f(E)^*)$ and equal norms for the operator and its adjoint; in particular $D(f(E))=D(\overline f(E))$ and
$\|f(E)x\|=\|\overline f(E)x\|$ for all such $x$. Moreover
$$\|f(E)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x,\qquad \langle x,f(E)x\rangle=\int\overline f\,dE_x\qquad(x\in D(f(E))),$$
and $(f(E))^*=\overline f(E)$; in particular $f(E)$ is self-adjoint whenever
$f$ takes real values. Finally, if $(g_n)$ are bounded $\Sigma$-measurable functions with
$|g_n|\le C|f|$ pointwise and $g_n\to f$ pointwise, then $g_n(E)x\to f(E)x$
for every $x\in D(f(E))$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field and let
$T:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) whose range $T(X)$ admits an ordered basis of
finite length ([[def-linear-basis]]). Then $T$ is compact
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a
normed space, let $Y$ be a Banach space ([[def-banach-space]]), and let
$T_n:X\to Y$, $n\in\mathbb N$, be compact operators
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]) with $\|T_n-T\|\to0$ for a bounded linear
operator $T:X\to Y$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-operator-norm]], [[def-metric-convergence]]). Then $T$ is compact.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ and $K$
be Hilbert spaces over the same real or complex scalar field and let $T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be compact
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then $T$ is trace class
([[def-trace-class-operator]]) if and only if there are families
$(u_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $H$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $K$, indexed by the positive
integers, with
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<+\infty$$
such that the zero-based sequence of finite-rank operators defined by $R_0=0$
and
$$R_m:=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\langle\cdot,u_j\rangle v_j\qquad(m\ge1)$$
converges to $T$ in operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-metric-convergence]]).  Here the displayed scalar series is, under the
library convention, the series of the sequence
$(\|u_{m+1}\|\,\|v_{m+1}\|)_{m\in\mathbb N}$. In that case
$$\|T\|_1=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|:\ R_m\to T\ \text{in operator norm}\Bigr\},$$
the infimum being over all such **nuclear representations** of $T$, with the
same zero-based shift understood in every displayed sum, and the
infimum is attained: using its positive-integer index set and padding finite rank by zeros,
the singular-value series
$T=\sum_{j\in J}s_j\langle\cdot,e_j\rangle f_j$ is a nuclear representation with
sum $\|T\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has
   $$\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$$
   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   without assuming that $H$ has a Hilbert basis;
3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace
   norm: for trace-class $S,T$ and scalars $a,b$,
   $\operatorname{tr}(aS+bT)=a\operatorname{tr}(S)+b\operatorname{tr}(T)$ and
   $|\operatorname{tr}(T)|\le\|T\|_1$.

after.claim: [Product basis and finite-prefix exhaustion] The tensors $e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ are orthonormal by [F1]. Their span is dense: approximate each factor of an elementary tensor by its finite basis truncation using [F3]; the tensor norm formula and the telescoping difference of two products show convergence of these approximations, and finite sums of elementary tensors are dense by [F1]. Every finite collection of words is contained in some $H_m^{\otimes N}$. Since each $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is bounded, its images of this dense word span are dense in its range. In the finite prefix, these images span precisely the finite Slater or orbit-sum basis of [F2]. A word in $\operatorname{orb}(n)$ uses only finitely many modes, and the orbit consists of distinct orthonormal product vectors, so its sum has norm squared $|\operatorname{orb}(n)|>0$. Thus its displayed normalization agrees in every larger prefix. The finite-prefix Slater vectors likewise agree in every larger prefix. Any pair of proposed occupation vectors lies in a common prefix, where [F2] gives orthogonality; the normalized vectors have norm one. Their span is dense in the sector by the projection argument, proving (a). The index sets are countable because they are countable unions of finite prefix index sets.

[Diagonal domain and self-adjointness] Write either sector in the orthonormal coordinates of step 1.1. The specified domain contains every finite coordinate vector, hence is dense. For a vector in that domain, Parseval makes the defining energy series converge. If $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain, with adjoint value $z$, testing against each $b_c^\sigma$ gives $z_c=E_cy_c$ because $E_c$ is real. Since $z$ is square summable, $\sum_c|E_cy_c|^2<\infty$, so $y$ belongs to the specified domain. Conversely, if that sum is finite, Cauchy-Schwarz applied to the square-summable coefficient families gives $\langle H_N^\sigma x,y\rangle=\langle x,H_N^\sigma y\rangle$ for every domain vector $x$, so $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain with the stated value. The domains and values agree, proving self-adjointness by [F3]. Since every $E_c\ge Nb$, the absolutely convergent energy quadratic sum is at least $Nb\|x\|^2$. Finite coordinate truncations converge in both norm and graph norm since both square-sum tails vanish, so finite occupation sums are a core and the operator is their diagonal closure.

[Labelled energy and spectral measure] The same coordinate-domain construction on the product-word basis defines a self-adjoint labelled operator with energies $\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k}$, agreeing with the free slot-energy sum on finite mode words. Every permutation of a word has the same energy, so its domain and action commute with each permutation unitary and the projections [F1]. Their sector restrictions have exactly the occupation energies and domain of step 2.1. For the displayed $E_N^\sigma(B)$, the projection and intersection identities follow coordinatewise; for disjoint $B_l$, the tails of the square-summable coordinates give strong countable additivity and total mass $I$, so it is a PVM. The scalar measure of a vector $\psi=\sum_ca_cb_c^\sigma$ is $\sum_c|a_c|^2\delta_{E_c}$, so [F4] gives the identity-integral domain exactly $\sum_cE_c^2|a_c|^2<\infty$; bounded spectral truncations converge to the displayed coordinate action there. This PVM is also uniquely determined by that operator: if another PVM represents it, the zero norm of $(H_N^\sigma-E_c)b_c^\sigma$ forces its scalar measure at $b_c^\sigma$ to be supported at $E_c$. Its projections therefore act as $\mathbf1_B(E_c)$ on every $b_c^\sigma$, and density gives equality on the whole sector. For the exponential, use the bounded Borel function $g(a)=e^{-\beta\max\{a,Nb\}}$ on $\mathbb R$; it agrees with $e^{-\beta a}$ on the support of this PVM. [F4] therefore gives the bounded positive operator with eigenvalues $e^{-\beta E_c}\le e^{-\beta Nb}$, namely $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$. This proves (b) and identifies the exponential used in (c).

[Extended trace and occupation sums] Put $r_c:=e^{-\beta E_c}$, a bounded positive family. In the supplied occupation basis the extended positive trace is $\sum_cr_c$. This value is basis independent even when infinite: if $(v_l)$ is any other orthonormal basis, then $\sum_l\langle e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}v_l,v_l\rangle=\sum_l\sum_cr_c|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=\sum_cr_c$, since nonnegative-series sums can be interchanged as suprema over finite subsums, and Parseval gives $\sum_l|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=1$. A Bose occupation sequence has a unique sorted word $i_1\le\cdots\le i_N$, and a Fermi subset has a unique increasing word; $e^{-\beta E_c}$ is the product of the corresponding $q_j$. Thus the trace equals $h_N(q)$ or $e_N(q)$ as stated. If the sum is finite, the series of rank-one operators $\sum_cr_c\langle\cdot,b_c^\sigma\rangle b_c^\sigma$ is nuclear and converges in operator norm to the exponential: its norm tail is at most the summable scalar tail. Its finite-rank partial sums and [F5] first give compactness, and the nuclear criterion then gives trace class and the ordinary trace formula. Conversely trace class forces the diagonal sum to be finite by [F5].

[Upper and lower bounds and finiteness] Let $Q:=\sum_jq_j\in(0,\infty]$. The sum over all ordered words of length $N$ is $Q^N$: on the first $m$ modes it is $(\sum_{j\le m}q_j)^N$, and every finite collection of words is contained in one such prefix. The nondecreasing and strictly increasing index sets are subsets of the ordered-word set, giving $Z_N^\sigma\le Q^N$. For $N\ge2$, configurations selecting modes $1,\ldots,N-1$ once each and one additional mode $j\ge N$ are valid for both statistics, distinct as $j$ varies, and have weight $(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k)q_j$. Their sum gives the lower bound. For $N=1$, every configuration is the single mode $j$, so both traces equal $Q$; the empty product is $1$ and the tail starts at $1$. For any $N$, the lower-bound coefficient is strictly positive and finite, and the omitted initial segment of $Q$ is finite. Hence $Q=\infty$ forces $Z_N^\sigma=\infty$, whereas $Q<\infty$ gives $Z_N^\sigma<\infty$ by the upper bound. The single configuration $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has positive weight for either sign, so both traces are strictly positive. This proves all of (c). No sum over particle numbers or full-Fock product formula is used.

[Upper and lower bounds and finiteness] Let $Q:=\sum_jq_j\in(0,\infty]$. The sum over all ordered words of length $N$ is $Q^N$: on the first $m$ modes it is $(\sum_{j\le m}q_j)^N$, and every finite collection of words is contained in one such prefix. The nondecreasing and strictly increasing index sets are subsets of the ordered-word set, giving $Z_N^\sigma\le Q^N$. For $N\ge2$, configurations selecting modes $1,\ldots,N-1$ once each and one additional mode $j\ge N$ are valid for both statistics, distinct as $j$ varies, and have weight $(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k)q_j$. For any $N$, the lower-bound coefficient is strictly positive and finite, and the omitted initial segment of $Q$ is finite. Hence $Q=\infty$ forces $Z_N^\sigma=\infty$, whereas $Q<\infty$ gives $Z_N^\sigma<\infty$ by the upper bound. The single configuration $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has positive weight for either sign, so both traces are strictly positive. This proves all of (c). No sum over particle numbers or full-Fock product formula is used.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E_A$ be its spectral PVM, let $\rho$ be a density operator, and set $\mu_\rho^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$. Then:

(a) The finite first mean is defined exactly under the absolute-first-moment condition
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)<\infty,$$
and its value is $m:=\int a\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)$. For every positive-eigenvalue expansion $\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a), with $w_k>0$ and $\sum_kw_k=1$, one has
$$\int|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A=\sum_kw_k\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k},\qquad m=\sum_kw_k\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}.$$
The first identity allows infinity; the second is asserted under the stated integrability condition and converges absolutely. This condition does not require $u_k\in D(A)$.

(b) If $A$ is bounded, the condition in (a) holds automatically and
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A).$$

(c) Suppose the condition in (a) holds and the **literal product** $A\rho$ is defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class; thus $\rho(H)\subset D(A)$ and $T:=A\rho\in\mathcal S_1(H)$. Then
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(T).$$
Moreover the densely defined product $\rho A$ has bounded closure $T^*$, that closure is trace class, and $\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho A})=m$. This is a conditional trace identity for defined trace-class products. The existence of the mean alone does not assert any of these unbounded-operator product hypotheses.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The choice hypotheses, $A,E_A,\rho,\mu_\rho^A$, and in (c) the explicitly stated literal-product assumptions.

[F1] The density eigenexpansion has positive weights and orthonormal vectors, converges in trace norm, and gives $\mu_\rho^A(B)=\sum_kw_kE_{A,u_k}(B)$. For $u\in D(A)$, $\int a\,dE_{A,u}=\langle Au,u\rangle$; absolute first integrability alone is equivalent to $u\in D(|A|^{1/2})$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a)-(c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; integrate the density eigenexpansion and compare it with correctly defined trace products.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then for every bounded $B$

$$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. No cyclic permutation of unbounded operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has
   $$\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$$
   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   without assuming that $H$ has a Hilbert basis;
3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace
   norm: for trace-class $S,T$ and scalars $a,b$,
   $\operatorname{tr}(aS+bT)=a\operatorname{tr}(S)+b\operatorname{tr}(T)$ and
   $|\operatorname{tr}(T)|\le\|T\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ and $K$
be Hilbert spaces over the same real or complex scalar field and let $T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be compact
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then $T$ is trace class
([[def-trace-class-operator]]) if and only if there are families
$(u_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $H$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $K$, indexed by the positive
integers, with
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<+\infty$$
such that the zero-based sequence of finite-rank operators defined by $R_0=0$
and
$$R_m:=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\langle\cdot,u_j\rangle v_j\qquad(m\ge1)$$
converges to $T$ in operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-metric-convergence]]).  Here the displayed scalar series is, under the
library convention, the series of the sequence
$(\|u_{m+1}\|\,\|v_{m+1}\|)_{m\in\mathbb N}$. In that case
$$\|T\|_1=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|:\ R_m\to T\ \text{in operator norm}\Bigr\},$$
the infimum being over all such **nuclear representations** of $T$, with the
same zero-based shift understood in every displayed sum, and the
infimum is attained: using its positive-integer index set and padding finite rank by zeros,
the singular-value series
$T=\sum_{j\in J}s_j\langle\cdot,e_j\rangle f_j$ is a nuclear representation with
sum $\|T\|_1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(P, \le)$ be a
nonempty poset in which **every chain has an upper bound**. Then $P$ has a
maximal element ([[def-maximal-element]]).

Note the hypothesis asks only for an upper bound, not a least upper bound, and
the conclusion asserts only that a maximal element exists, never that a greatest
one does.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be an orthonormal family in a real or complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), and
for $x\in H$ and finite $F\subseteq I$ put

$$P_Fx:=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i .$$

Then the following four assertions are equivalent:

1. **(completeness)** the closed linear span of $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ is $H$;
2. **(zero complement)** the only vector orthogonal to every $e_i$ is $0$;
3. **(Parseval)** $\displaystyle\sum_{i\in I}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2=\|x\|^2$
   for every $x\in H$, the sum being the supremum of the finite subsums
   ([[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]);
4. **(net convergence)** the finite-subset net $(P_Fx)_{F\in\operatorname{Fin}(I)}$
   converges to $x$ for every $x\in H$.

Assertion 2 is the statement
$\operatorname{span}\{e_i : i\in I\}^\perp=\{0\}$
([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be a complete orthonormal family in a real or complex Hilbert
space $H$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]) and
let $x\in H$, with partial sums
$P_Fx=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i$ over finite $F\subseteq I$. Then:

1. $x$ is the norm limit of the finite-subset net $(P_Fx)$, that is
   $$x=\sum_{i\in I}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i$$
   in the sense of convergence of the net of finite subsums;
2. **the coefficients are unique**: if $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ is a family in
   $\mathbb F$ whose finite-subset net $\sum_{i\in F}a_ie_i$ converges to $x$,
   then $a_i=\langle x,e_i\rangle$ for every $i\in I$;
3. the support $\{i : \langle x,e_i\rangle\ne0\}$ is at most countable, and the
   expansion does not depend on an ordering: if $(i_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ is a
   sequence of pairwise distinct elements of $I$ whose image contains the
   support, then the sequence of partial sums
   $\sum_{k<n}\langle x,e_{i_k}\rangle e_{i_k}$ also converges to $x$.

Claim 3 is the sense in which the expansion is **unconditional**: the sum is
independent of any ordering, because the finite-subset net converges and any
enumeration of a set containing the support by pairwise distinct indices is
cofinal in the squared mass.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field and let
$T:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) whose range $T(X)$ admits an ordered basis of
finite length ([[def-linear-basis]]). Then $T$ is compact
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a
normed space, let $Y$ be a Banach space ([[def-banach-space]]), and let
$T_n:X\to Y$, $n\in\mathbb N$, be compact operators
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]) with $\|T_n-T\|\to0$ for a bounded linear
operator $T:X\to Y$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-operator-norm]], [[def-metric-convergence]]). Then $T$ is compact.

Complete the orthonormal eigenfamily by an orthonormal basis of its perpendicular subspace using the already assumed AC. The density eigenexpansion shows $\rho=0$ on that perpendicular subspace, so $T=0$ there. The trace diagonal formula [F4] therefore gives $\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_k\langle Tu_k,u_k\rangle=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$. ## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4), the non-relativistic kinematics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state
reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable
reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
Let a **declared species sector** with one-particle space $H$, mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ be given as in that definition, in the massive spin-$s$
one-particle reading of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; fix an integer
$N\ge1$ and let $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq
H^{\otimes N}$ be the declared $N$-particle sector. All quantities below are
read in the SI conventions and units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (energies in joules). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is assumed only in the Coulomb realization of
clause (d)(ii), where it is the choice hypothesis of the cited self-adjointness
theorem.

**(b) Declared one-particle data.** The model declares a one-particle
**energy operator** in one of the two following realizations.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. A more singular declared
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}$, such as $-g/|x|$, is used only through a separate
self-adjointness statement, which the model must supply before the operator is
read as an observable.

(ii) *Finite-mode realization.* A finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
$K$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with a declared orthonormal basis
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) is declared together with a
self-adjoint **one-particle operator** $h\in\mathcal B(K)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
Here the one-particle space of the species is $K$, and the assignment of the
modes $f_j$ to a laboratory mode family is a tested identification under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not part of the definition.

**(c) Declared interaction.** The model declares a **pair interaction** in the
matching realization.

(i) *Bounded interaction.* In the spatial realization let
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be real, measurable, bounded with
$W(-z)=W(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\|W\|_\infty<\infty$. In the
finite-mode realization let $W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ be
self-adjoint with $U_{(12)}WU_{(12)}=W$, where $U_{(12)}$ is the exchange
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (a)
in the tensor square $\widehat{K\otimes K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. The interaction strength
constants entering $W$ are empirical model parameters with their uncertainties
in the sense of P6 clause (iii).

(ii) *Coulomb interaction.* In the spatial realization the model may declare
the singular pair interaction $W(z):=\kappa/|z|$ with a real coupling
$\kappa\in\mathbb R$ (repulsive for $\kappa>0$), and an external
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}(x):=-g/|x|$ with $g\in\mathbb R$; the combined singular
multiplier is that of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]].

**(d) The labelled energy operator and its sector restriction.** Fix the
particle masses $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ of the declared species.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* With $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$
the Euclidean product unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], form the labelled
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clause (b)
whose potential is
$V(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$; by that theorem
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] the
transported projections $\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}$ reduce
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and the restriction
$$H_N^\sigma:=\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)H_{\mathrm{lab}}\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)\big|_{\operatorname{ran}(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1})}$$
is a self-adjoint operator on the transported sector; the model identifies it
with the restriction of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ to
$\Theta^{-1}$-transported $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the tensor reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* With the singular data of clause (c)(ii), the
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_V$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clause (b)
is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and
bounded below, and by clause (d) of that theorem its restrictions to the
symmetric and antisymmetric sectors are self-adjoint; the model's sector
energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ is that restriction, with the same reading as in
(i).

(iii) *Finite-mode case.* On $K^{\otimes N}$ put

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (finite sum in the
finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

## Remarks

- **Why the finite case first.** In the finite-dimensional sector the entropy
  is an ordinary finite sum over $D$ eigenvalues, and the comparison theorem
  of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] is
  available without any trace-class convergence hypothesis on
  $\rho\log\rho$. The infinite-dimensional questions are deferred rather than
  assumed.
- **Units of $\beta$.** $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ has the unit
  $\mathrm J^{-1}\mathrm K\,\mathrm K^{-1}=\mathrm J^{-1}$, so the exponent
  $\beta H_N^\sigma$ is dimensionless, as the spectral calculus requires.

## Postulate

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with a
declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and the entropy,
Boltzmann-constant and free-energy vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Let
$H_N^\sigma$ be the model's sector energy operator with spectral
projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), assume it is bounded below, let $T>0$ be
an assigned temperature in kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in
$\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned Boltzmann constant $k_B$ of the entropy
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** Assume the
**partition sum is finite**:
$$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\beta\lambda}\,d\bigl(\operatorname{tr}E(\lambda)\bigr)<\infty .$$
Then $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is defined by the spectral calculus of the
self-adjoint generator, it is positive with finite trace $Z_N>0$, and the
model adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared
model at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}.$$
In the finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition, $Z_N$ is
the finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues and $\rho_\beta$
is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]; the
hypothesis $Z_N<\infty$ is automatic there. Outside that class the
hypothesis is a genuine restriction: the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] exhibits the
case $Z_N=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, and the product criterion of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]] shows that
countably many free modes have finite $Z_N$ exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$.

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ of the system whose mean in $\rho_\beta$ exists
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)),
the number
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$$
is the model's **thermal mean** of $A$ at temperature $T$, read in the unit
$u_A$; when the mean does not exist the model asserts no thermal mean. The
identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the free-energy functional. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $Z_N<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when the
partition sum diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

## Remarks

- **The finite-sector case.** For a finite-dimensional sector the existence
  hypothesis is a finite sum and hence automatic; the only content of clause
  (b) there is the assignment of the Gibbs weights to the declared energies.
- **Relation to P4.** The postulate adds a preparation assumption to the
  dynamics; by itself P4 describes the unitary evolution of whatever
  preparation is declared, and does not single out $\rho_\beta$. The precise
  sense in which unitary evolution cannot produce $\rho_\beta$ from a
  different preparation is a separate theorem of this pair.

## Postulate

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

## Remarks

- **The finite-sector case.** For a nonzero finite-dimensional sector the existence
  hypothesis is a positive finite sum and hence automatic (and likewise for
  any separately declared nonzero finite-dimensional mode space); the only content of clause
  (b) there is the assignment of the Gibbs weights to the declared energies.
- **Relation to P4.** The postulate adds a preparation assumption to the
  dynamics; by itself P4 describes the unitary evolution of whatever
  preparation is declared, and does not single out $\rho_\beta$. The precise
  sense in which unitary evolution cannot produce $\rho_\beta$ from a
  different preparation is a separate theorem of this pair.

physical_scope.after: The adopted equilibrium-ensemble assumption of the many-body pair: for a declared fixed-N model or a separately declared number-variable mode model with self-adjoint semibounded Gibbs generator G (including a declared effective generator H-mu N), assigned temperature and strictly positive finite partition trace, the Gibbs preparation rho_beta = e^{-beta G}/Z, its thermal means, and the identifications of beta = 1/(k_B T) and of rho_beta with the model's description of thermal equilibrium. It is an adopted statistical-mechanical assumption motivated by maximum-entropy reasoning, not a consequence of the framework's state, probability or dynamics postulates; it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration rate, no thermodynamic limit and no fact about a laboratory sample except through the tested identifications of P7.

The theorem is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P6, on the adopted finite-mode idealization and on the declared one-particle Hamiltonian; it asserts no interaction, no spatial or infinite-mode result, no thermal state, no thermodynamic limit and no laboratory identification.

derivations.claim: [The labelled operator on the product basis] By [F2] each $h^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$. On the product basis vector $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ the $i$-th slot operator acts as $h$ on the factor $e_{i_k}$, giving $h^{(k)}e_i=\varepsilon_{i_k}e_i$; hence $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k})e_i$. Since every $U_\pi$ permutes the slots and $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is the sum over all slots, $U_\pi H_{\mathrm{lab}}U_\pi^*=H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

[Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

[Partition sum and ground energy] The trace of $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is the sum of $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ over the eigenvalues with multiplicity, read on the orthogonal sector bases of step 2.1: $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$ over the occupation configurations of clause (c), a finite nonempty sum of positive numbers for $\sigma=+$ and for $\sigma=-$ with $N\le d$, and empty (no sector states) for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$. If $\sigma=-$, then for every configuration $\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d$ with $\sum\lambda_j=N$ the support $J=\operatorname{supp}\lambda$ has $N$ elements and $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j\ge\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ because the latter is the sum of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues; equality holds exactly for $J$ the set of indices of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues. If $\sigma=+$, then $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\ge\varepsilon_{(1)}\sum_j\lambda_j=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, with equality exactly when every occupied mode has eigenvalue $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally, expanding a unit $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the orthogonal sector basis of step 2.1 gives $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2\lambda_\lambda\ge E_0$ with the stated equality case, where the coefficients are normalized. This proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

[Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. By [F5] and step 2.1 each such $\Psi$ is an eigenvector of the generator, so its pure preparation is stationary under the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ with $\Psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\Psi$, and the energy law of any preparation is the finite spectral law in the sector basis. This proves (d). [F5, step 2.1, algebra]

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), step 3.1 proves (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

N=1 reduces to the one-particle operator on the sector K itself; the formulas lambda_J and lambda_lambda specialise to the one-particle eigenvalues, and the ground-energy expressions match after sorting.

Repeated one-particle eigenvalues are handled by counting configurations: every occupation configuration produces its eigenvalue, degenerate sector eigenvalues are not further resolved, and only the partition sum over configurations is asserted.
The boundary case N=d for sigma=- leaves a one-dimensional antisymmetric sector and is included; N>d is excluded as above; beta>0 is strict in clause (c).
Countable Choice is used through the occupation-basis and tensor suppliers; the Axiom of Choice is not needed for this finite-dimensional statement.
