Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field $\mathbb K$, read in
the real case from [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from
[[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]. A linear map
$T:X\to Y$ ([[def-linear-map]]) is a **bounded linear operator** when there is a
real constant $C \ge 0$ such that

$$\|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \qquad \text{for all } x \in X.$$

Any such $C$ is called a **bound** for $T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\sigma(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\sigma(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\},\ |J|=n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\rho_i(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H^{\otimes n}$ and
$P_\pm^{(n)}$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (with
$P_\pm^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$), and let $W(n,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$
and $m_\lambda$ be the symmetric vectors of that theorem. Then:

(a) *fermionic configurations*: the map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection
from the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ onto the set
$\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$; consequently
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\#\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_j=n\},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{d}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=2^{d};$$

(b) *bosonic configurations*: the assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ induces
a bijection from $W(n,d)$ onto the set of lines spanned by the orthogonal basis
$(m_\lambda)$, so the number of bosonic configurations of total occupation
exactly $n$ is $\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$, and for every $N\ge0$ the
number of bosonic configurations of total occupation at most $N$ is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d};$$

(c) *exclusion counts*: no fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$, so the
antisymmetric Slater index set contains no $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j\ge2$ for
some $j$; for $n>d$ there is no fermionic configuration at all and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$, while for every $n$ and every $j$ the
bosonic configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ occurs, so
no occupation bound holds in the symmetric sector;

(d) *consistency with the total occupation*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ one
has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, and for every fermionic configuration
$\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ likewise; in particular the
total occupation equals the particle number $n$ in both sectors.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and write $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. Then:

(a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and the second moment of the energy law of $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent, with time-zero values $\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle$ and $\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}$; if one of these moments is infinite at time zero, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(c) **Stationary states are exactly the eigenrays.** Let $\psi\in H$, $\psi\ne0$. The pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, if and only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $\psi\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. In that case $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi(0)$ for every $t$, and every assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law in this preparation: $\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)$ for every $(A,u_A)$, every Borel $B$ and every $t$.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** No equilibration, relaxation, decay or convergence of the law of an arbitrary preparation is asserted; no moment beyond those finite at time zero is claimed; the converse of (b) — constancy of the law of a bounded observable in every preparation implying strong spectral compatibility with the energy — is not asserted for a general (possibly unbounded) $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; and the item is conditional on the isolated-system idealization of P4, asserting no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has
   $$\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$$
   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   without assuming that $H$ has a Hilbert basis;
3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace
   norm: for trace-class $S,T$ and scalars $a,b$,
   $\operatorname{tr}(aS+bT)=a\operatorname{tr}(S)+b\operatorname{tr}(T)$ and
   $|\operatorname{tr}(T)|\le\|T\|_1$.

before.claim: [The labelled operator on the product basis] By [F2] each $h^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$. On the product basis vector $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ the $i$-th slot operator acts as $h$ on the factor $e_{i_k}$, giving $h^{(k)}e_i=\varepsilon_{i_k}e_i$; hence $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k})e_i$. Since every $U_\pi$ permutes the slots and $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is the sum over all slots, $U_\pi H_{\mathrm{lab}}U_\pi^*=H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

[Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

[Partition sum and ground energy] The trace of $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is the sum of $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ over the eigenvalues with multiplicity, read on the orthogonal sector bases of step 2.1: $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$ over the occupation configurations of clause (c), a finite nonempty sum of positive numbers for $\sigma=+$ and for $\sigma=-$ with $N\le d$, and empty (no sector states) for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$. If $\sigma=-$, then for every configuration $\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d$ with $\sum\lambda_j=N$ the support $J=\operatorname{supp}\lambda$ has $N$ elements and $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j\ge\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ because the latter is the sum of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues; equality holds exactly for $J$ the set of indices of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues. If $\sigma=+$, then $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\ge\varepsilon_{(1)}\sum_j\lambda_j=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, with equality exactly when every occupied mode has eigenvalue $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally, expanding a unit $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the orthogonal sector basis of step 2.1 gives $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2\lambda_\lambda\ge E_0$ with the stated equality case, where the coefficients are normalized. This proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

[Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. By [F5] and step 2.1 each such $\Psi$ is an eigenvector of the generator, so its pure preparation is stationary under the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ with $\Psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\Psi$, and the energy law of any preparation is the finite spectral law in the sector basis. This proves (d). [F5, step 2.1, algebra]

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), step 3.1 proves (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. This proves (b).

[Partition sum and the zero sector] Normalize the symmetric vectors to $\widetilde m_\lambda:=m_\lambda/\|m_\lambda\|$; by [F3] these form an orthonormal eigenbasis, as do the Slater vectors in the fermionic sector. The trace is therefore $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$, with the configuration counts $M_N^-=\binom dN$ and $M_N^+=\binom{N+d-1}{N}$ from [F4]. For $\sigma=-$, $N>d$, the index set is empty and the trace is the empty sum $0$. There is no eigenvector on $\{0\}$ and hence no ground eigenvalue, and its only operator has trace $0$, so no trace-one density or normalized Gibbs density exists there. In every other case [F4] gives a finite nonempty index set, so its finite sum of positive Boltzmann weights has $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$. For that case finite minima and maxima $E_0,E_{\max}$ exist, and for each configuration $e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}\le e^{-\beta E_0}$, because $\beta>0$; summing the $M_N^\sigma$ inequalities proves the two bounds. [Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. This proves (d).

[Extreme energies and ground eigenspace] Work on a nonzero sector. For $\sigma=-$, each configuration selects $N$ distinct eigenvalues, so its energy is at least the sum of the $N$ smallest and at most the sum of the $N$ largest; these bounds are attained by the corresponding subsets. Thus $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and $E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)}$. A minimizing subset contains every mode with energy strictly below $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, contains no mode with energy strictly above $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, and fills its remaining places with modes at that boundary energy; this includes all choices allowed by degeneracy. For $\sigma=+$, the identity $\sum_j\lambda_j=N$ gives $N\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\le N\varepsilon_{(d)}$; the two bounds are attained by putting all particles in a minimum-energy or maximum-energy mode respectively. Equality at the lower bound holds exactly when every occupied mode has energy $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally expand a unit vector in the orthonormal sector basis of step 3.1: $\psi=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$, $\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2=1$. Then $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle-E_0=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2(\lambda_\lambda-E_0)\ge0$, with equality exactly when all coefficients at energies greater than $E_0$ vanish, that is, exactly on the ground eigenspace. anchors.claim_quote:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index

eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of

stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and

spectral sum in the sector basis;

step_quotes.quote: 4.1 [Extreme energies and ground eigenspace] Work on a nonzero sector. For $\sigma=-$, each configuration selects $N$ distinct eigenvalues, so its energy is at least the sum of the $N$ smallest and at most the sum of the $N$ largest; these bounds are attained by the corresponding subsets. Thus $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and $E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)}$. A minimizing subset contains every mode with energy strictly below $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, contains no mode with energy strictly above $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, and fills its remaining places with modes at that boundary energy; this includes all choices allowed by degeneracy. For $\sigma=+$, the identity $\sum_j\lambda_j=N$ gives $N\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\le N\varepsilon_{(d)}$; the two bounds are attained by putting all particles in a minimum-energy or maximum-energy mode respectively. Equality at the lower bound holds exactly when every occupied mode has energy $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally expand a unit vector in the orthonormal sector basis of step 3.1: $\psi=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$, $\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2=1$. Then $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle-E_0=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2(\lambda_\lambda-E_0)\ge0$, with equality exactly when all coefficients at energies greater than $E_0$ vanish, that is, exactly on the ground eigenspace. Together with step 3.1 this proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited tensor, permutation and trace suppliers. Work in the finite-mode
realization of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-one-body-reduced-operator]]:
one-particle space $K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with modes
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: if $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ are pairwise
orthonormal and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ the Slater
vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (a) for $\sigma=-$, or $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$
for $\sigma=+$ (both unit vectors of the sector), then
$\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle;$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-mode sector data of the statement, the self-adjoint $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with unit $u_O$, and a declared sector preparation $\rho$.

[F1] **Sector vocabulary.** $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is a closed subspace of $K^{\otimes N}$; every permutation unitary $U_\pi$ preserves it and acts there as the scalar $\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)$; a declared sector preparation is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ ([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]] clauses (c)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Slot operators and reduction.** For $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,N\}$ the slot operator $O^{(i)}$ satisfies $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, and $(O^{(i)})^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$; $\Sigma(O)=\sum_iO^{(i)}$ commutes with every $U_\pi$ and with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, preserves the sectors, and for every sector preparation $\rho$ with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$, where $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator on $K$ ([[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] clauses (a), (c), (d), (e)).

[F3] **Observable reading and moments.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ has outcome law $\mu^A_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$; for a bounded self-adjoint $A$ and every preparation $\rho$ the mean exists and equals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$, and for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (d), [[prop-trace-is-linear]], [[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F4] **Slater and symmetric product vectors.** For pairwise orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_N$ the Slater vector $S(u_1,\dots,u_N)=N!^{-1/2}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(N)}$ has norm one and equals $\sqrt{N!}\,P_-^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clauses (a), (b)); setting $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$, orthonormality gives $\langle P_+^{(N)}x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\langle U_\sigma x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\langle x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}$, so $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}x$ is a unit vector of the symmetric sector with $P_+^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F5] **Rank-one pairing.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$ and $T_{u,v}^*=T_{v,u}$; the map $(u,v)\mapsto T_{u,v}$ is linear in $u$ and conjugate-linear in $v$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the sector sum as a bounded observable, apply the supplied reduction identity, and evaluate the product-type cases by orthonormality of the mode family.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3]. [F2, F3, def. bounded, algebra]

1.2 [Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. For fixed $\tau$, $\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_{\tau^{-1}(i)},u_i\rangle\prod_{k\ne i}\langle u_{\tau^{-1}(k)},u_k\rangle$ by [F1] and the elementary-tensor pairing, and orthonormality makes every factor $\delta_{\tau^{-1}(k),k}$ vanish unless $\tau=\mathrm{id}$; hence only the identity permutation contributes and $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_i,u_i\rangle$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. Since $A_O$ is bounded, [F3] gives $m_\rho(A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)$, and by steps 1.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (a) and (b). [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. Testing the resulting identity $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$ against $O=T_{u,v}$ and using [F5], $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma_\rho u,v\rangle$ and $N^{-1}\sum_j\langle T_{u,v}u_j,u_j\rangle=N^{-1}\sum_j\langle u_j,v\rangle\langle u,u_j\rangle$; the identity for all $u,v$ therefore gives $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$, since two endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional space with equal pairings against every rank-one operator are equal. This proves (c). [F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a) and (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The factor $N$ and the normalization of $\gamma_\rho$.** The reduced preparation is normalized as a probability state on the one-particle space, while $A_O$ sums $N$ slot terms; the product-type case shows the two conventions consistently: a Slater determinant of $N$ orthonormal modes has reduced preparation the equal-weight mixture of those modes.
- **No separability claim.** The mean law holds for arbitrary sector preparations, entangled or not; nothing in the argument factors $\rho$, and the product-type clause is a special case.

- **The factor $N$ and the normalization of $\gamma_\rho$.** The reduced preparation is normalized as a probability state on the one-particle space, while $A_O$ sums $N$ slot terms; the product-type case shows the two conventions consistently: a Slater determinant of $N$ orthonormal modes has reduced preparation the equal-weight mixture of those modes.
- **No separability claim.** The mean law holds for arbitrary sector preparations, entangled or not; nothing in the argument factors $\rho$, and the product-type clause is a special case.

physical_scope.after: The conditional one-body readout law of the declared finite-mode many-body model: for a bounded self-adjoint one-particle quantity the summed sector operator is an assigned sharp observable, its mean in every declared sector preparation exists and is N times the pairing of the one-body reduced preparation with the quantity, and for declared Slater and orthonormal-mode symmetric preparations the reduced preparation is the equal-weight mixture of the occupied modes. The theorem is conditional on P1, P2 and P6, the adopted finite-mode idealization and the declared preparation; it asserts no measured mean, no individual-particle property, no separability of the sector state and no spatial (infinite-mode) reduction.

derivations.claim: [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3]. [F2, F3, def. bounded, algebra]

[Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. For fixed $\tau$, $\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_{\tau^{-1}(i)},u_i\rangle\prod_{k\ne i}\langle u_{\tau^{-1}(k)},u_k\rangle$ by [F1] and the elementary-tensor pairing, and orthonormality makes every factor $\delta_{\tau^{-1}(k),k}$ vanish unless $\tau=\mathrm{id}$; hence only the identity permutation contributes and $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_i,u_i\rangle$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

[The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. Since $A_O$ is bounded, [F3] gives $m_\rho(A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)$, and by steps 1.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (a) and (b). [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

[Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. Testing the resulting identity $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$ against $O=T_{u,v}$ and using [F5], $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma_\rho u,v\rangle$ and $N^{-1}\sum_j\langle T_{u,v}u_j,u_j\rangle=N^{-1}\sum_j\langle u_j,v\rangle\langle u,u_j\rangle$; the identity for all $u,v$ therefore gives $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$, since two endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional space with equal pairings against every rank-one operator are equal. This proves (c). [F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a) and (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

boundaries.reason: The one-particle space is finite-dimensional with d>=1 modes and N>=1 particles, so no empty tensor or sector space arises in the clauses; the rank-one testing operators O=T_{u,v} are bounded and pose no domain question.

boundaries.evidence: O=0 gives the zero readout with mean 0=N tr(gamma 0); X and its algebra in the product clause are used only through the bounded operator X and its pairing.
For N=1 the readout is O itself, gamma_rho=rho by the reduction lemma with no factors traced, and the mean law reads m=N tr(rho O)=tr(rho O).

The product-type clause assumes pairwise orthonormal u_1,...,u_N; repeated modes are excluded there, and for repetitions the Slater vector vanishes while the symmetric vector needs separate normalisation.
The stated law is for every declared sector preparation, pure or mixed; the product clause covers both sectors with the normalisation constants sqrt(N!) of the two projections.
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are used as the hypotheses of the trace, permutation and tensor suppliers; step 1.2 uses only finite sums.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$; for $n=1$ the
empty product is $1\in\mathbb C$ and $J_1u=u\otimes1$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), let $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow H^{\otimes n}$ be
the isometric inclusion and define its zero extension
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; then
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\bigl(J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}\bigr)\in\mathcal B(H)$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names; for $n=1$, $\gamma=\rho$. If
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\{0\}$, there is no density operator of trace one on
that sector, so clauses (d)-(e) make no assertion about a sector preparation;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$; the second moment is $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}\in[0,\infty]$, finite if and only if $u_n\in D(A)$ for every $n$ of positive weight. More generally the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] shows that whenever the means are finite the mean of a statistical mixture is the weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric
projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]],

satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and
$S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$;

(b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then
$P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d));

(c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and
bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let
$\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the
Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put
$\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and
$$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$
integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the
pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is
$$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$

(d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$,
$X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently
$D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower
expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction.

The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it
does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the
spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No
physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

before.claim: [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3]. [F2, F3, def. bounded, algebra]

[Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. [Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (c). [F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

anchors.claim_quote:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited tensor, permutation and trace suppliers. Work in the finite-mode
realization of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-one-body-reduced-operator]]:
one-particle space $K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with modes
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: if $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ are pairwise
orthonormal and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ the Slater
vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (a) for $\sigma=-$, or $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$
for $\sigma=+$ (both unit vectors of the sector), then
$\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle;$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

with $h_1$ the declared one-particle operator and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\star$
the $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ pairing, and let $D$ and $X$ be the direct and
exchange integrals
$$D=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (c). Let $\chi_-$ be the spin singlet, $\chi_+$ the symmetric
$S_z=0$ triplet vector of the spin-$\tfrac12$ factor, and let
$$\Phi_-:=(\varphi_-\otimes\chi_+),\qquad \varphi_-:=(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,$$
$$\Phi_+:=(\varphi_+\otimes\chi_-),\qquad \varphi_+:=(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,$$

**Proof technique:** direct; exhibit the two sector vectors, split the energy expectation into its one-body and pair parts using spin independence, and insert the supplied direct and exchange integrals.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Domain membership and the one-body expectation] Both $u$ and $v$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, so $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ by [F5]; tensoring with the smooth spin vectors and transporting by $\Theta$ and the spin identification places $\Phi_\pm$ in the domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ of [F4]. - **What the exchange term is.** $X$ is the integral of the overlap density $\overline uv$ against its translate; it is not an interaction between distinguishable particles, and its sign in the repulsive-Coulomb case is the content of clause (c).
