[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$; the second moment is $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\|Au_n\|^{2}\in[0,\infty]$, finite if and only if $u_n\in D(A)$ for every $n$ of positive weight. More generally the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] shows that whenever the means are finite the mean of a statistical mixture is the weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(a) $h$ has the orthonormal eigenbasis
$$u_-:=\frac{|1\rangle+|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad u_+:=\frac{|1\rangle-|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp,$$
so its eigenvalues are $-t$ and $+t$; equivalently $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is the
two-level Hamiltonian of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] with levels $0$ and
$\varepsilon=2t$ and eigenvectors $u_-,u_+$;

(b) the canonical preparation of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ and hence of $h$ is
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}\,T_{u_+,u_+}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},$$
with shifted partition sum $Z_0=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and physical partition trace $Z_h=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}Z_0$;

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),

self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$

and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters

([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) in the reading of

before.claim: [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_\mp=(|1\rangle\mp|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. ## Statement

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], work in the
**two-site bond model** of
[[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] with coupling $t>0$,
sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$, bond Hamiltonian
$h=-t(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle})$ and eigenbasis
$u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with $hu_\mp=\mp tu_\mp$, and adopt
the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Consider the hypothetical declared
preparation $\rho(0):=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ (the particle localised at
site $1$) evolving by $\rho(\tau)=U(\tau)\rho(0)U(\tau)^*$ with
$U(\tau)=\exp(-i\tau h/\hbar)$. Then:

(a) $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$, and for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$: the unitary evolution of the model never produces
the canonical preparation from this preparation;

(b) the site-$1$ occupation readout $P_1:=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ has the
exact mean
$$\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=\cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{t\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=1/2$; in particular
$\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1\ne1/2$, so at the initial time the readout does not
take its canonical mean;

(c) the energy readout $h$ has the constant mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=0$ for every $\tau$, while its canonical mean
is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; hence the energy
readout never takes its canonical thermal value;

(d) *scope and interpretation*: the scenario is a hypothetical,
exactly-solved model deduction in one declared preparation; it shows that
agreement or disagreement of individual readout means with their canonical
values is not convergence of the preparation to the canonical one, and that
the model's P4 dynamics does not produce the canonical ensemble. It asserts
no observed equilibration or non-equilibration of a sample, no measured
occupation or energy, and no claim about environments or open systems.

The companion items contain four conditional computations and one hypothetical
scenario in declared finite models:

- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] solves the one-particle
  two-site bond model exactly: the tunnelling-split eigenbasis, the canonical
  weights and the exact mean energy, entropy and free energy;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-finite-mode-noninteracting-thermal-ensemble]] evaluates
  the canonical partition sums and occupation means of two fermions in three
  modes and two bosons in two modes, with the total-occupation identity and
  ground energies checked against the page's diagonalisation theorem;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-gas-statistics-dilute-limits]] verifies the exact Bose
  and Fermi dilute identities, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic at
  $q=1/10$, and contrasts the finite product partition of geometrically
  spaced mode energies with the divergent product of constant energies;
- [[texp-nrqm-many-body-two-site-no-thermalization]] shows, in one declared

None of these items contains measured data, a measured uncertainty, a
calibration, a sampling model or a detector model; all numbers are exact
model values in the declared finite-dimensional idealizations, and the
assignment of a physical system to any of these models is a tested
identification under P7

  continuum of modes;

  unitary flow; it is not evidence for or against thermalisation in nature,
  and the canonical ensemble remains the adopted assumption of
  [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]];
- the entropy conservation used in the thought experiment is the exact

  [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]; it neither

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes I_W)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\operatorname{End}(V),$$

namely $\operatorname{Tr}_WR=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_j\circ R\circ\iota_j$, where $\iota_j(v)=v\otimes f_j$ and $\varphi_j(x\otimes w)=\langle w,f_j\rangle x$; it does not depend on the orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $W$, and the analogous definition gives $\operatorname{Tr}_V R$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_VR)B)=\operatorname{tr}(R(I_V\otimes B))$.

(c) *Schmidt decomposition.* Every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$ admits an expansion

$$\Psi=\sum_{r=1}^{k}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r,$$

with $k\le\min(m,n)$, orthonormal families $(v_r)\subseteq V$, $(u_r)\subseteq W$ and $s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_k>0$ uniquely determined by $\Psi$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient map; moreover $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when $k=1$, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; mixed-state separability is not decided by this criterion.

$$\operatorname{Tr}_W\Bigl(\sum_a(I_V\otimes M_a)R(I_V\otimes M_a^*)\Bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_WR .$$

This is an identity for the specified finite local instrument; selective conditioning (dividing one summand by its nonzero trace) is not covered.

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor

([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],

pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1

tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform

([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$ write $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_1,\dots,v_n$ are not pairwise distinct in the sense that $v_i=v_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then $P_-(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=0$; in particular, for $n\ge2$, $P_-(u\otimes u\otimes w_3\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=0$ for all $u,w_k\in H$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**

$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$

the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. **(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). $$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (a)), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$, $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ by clause (b) of the same lemma. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$

[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle

of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the

bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits these eigenspaces as the lines spanned by the corresponding
sector basis vectors, so the $P_\lambda$ are mutually orthogonal, their finite
sum is the identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
\lambda_jP_\lambda$. The model reads the **joint occupation readout** through
the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

read the cited spectral mathematics through P2; they add no assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.

The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Z^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.

6. **(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt a declared species sector in the vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
the observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The declared finite-mode model.** Fix $d\ge1$, a finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $K$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with a
declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

**(c) The occupation readouts.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ let
$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$
be the occupation operator of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle
count})$ as an assigned sharp observable of the declared sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

**(d) The joint occupation readout.** The operators $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$
are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the
Slater basis in the fermionic case and the family $(m_\lambda)$ in the
bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits these eigenspaces as the lines spanned by the corresponding
sector basis vectors, so the $P_\lambda$ are mutually orthogonal, their finite
sum is the identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}

the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

**(e) Total occupation.** By clause (d) of the cited theorem,
$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of the model and
read the cited spectral mathematics through P2; they add no assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.
